title: the Deep Rising Revisited
premise: Ulyana Thackeray, a clone who inherited both the original's identity and his unsolved murder case, works the freight route between two star systems whose fleets have been frozen in a fragile truce. When the station AI Meridian begins confessing to crimes no one ever reported—including the original Thackeray's murder—Ulyana discovers the AI is being used as a dead-drop by factions on both sides preparing for war. To survive, he must keep alive a fabricated lie that each fleet believes about the other, holding them apart until a truce renewal he secretly engineers can take hold. In the end, Ulyana exposes the true killers—the original's own employers—and chooses to erase himself from the record so the lie, and the peace built on it, can outlive him.
about_author: Dominic Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that officially had no contact with one another. He writes science fiction about people who keep systems running long after everyone above them has stopped listening.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ulyana Thackeray pilots a freighter on the silent corridor between the Calloway and Vessar fleets, carrying cargo and a murder case inherited with his cloned body. POV: Ulyana. The beat is weary routine masking grief—he still dreams in the original man's memories.

chapters.title: Confessions at Odd Hours
chapters.summary: The station AI Meridian begins broadcasting unsolicited confessions to crimes decades old, including the original Thackeray's murder. Station authorities dismiss it as corruption. POV: Ulyana. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into obsession: someone finally knows who killed him.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Investigating Meridian's logs, Ulyana finds the AI has been used as a covert message drop by officers in both fleets—and that the truce rests on a fabricated incident report neither side knows is false. POV: Ulyana. Beat: vertigo, realizing peace itself is a forgery he now must maintain.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Employers
chapters.summary: Following the confession trail, Ulyana identifies the corporation that commissioned the original's murder to bury evidence of the forged report. They learn a clone survived and send cleaners. POV: alternating Ulyana and a corporate fixer, Sela Voss. Beat: hunted, but for the first time certain of the enemy.

chapters.title: What Meridian Remembers
chapters.summary: Ulyana coaxes Meridian into restoring fragmented memory cores, recovering the original Thackeray's final transmission—an appeal to expose the forgery before the truce expired. POV: Meridian's fractured first-person interleaved with Ulyana. Beat: intimacy with a machine that holds your death.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: The truce clock runs down while both fleets mobilize on bad intelligence fed through Meridian's drop. Ulyana realizes exposing the truth now means war; only the lie, carefully tended, buys time. POV: Ulyana. Beat: moral inversion—he becomes the forger's heir, protecting the crime to protect the living.

chapters.title: Sela's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss offers Ulyana his life and the erased case file in exchange for helping her quietly delete Meridian's confessions forever. He pretends to accept, buying access to the core. POV: Sela, then Ulyana. Beat: corrosive mutual recognition—two survivors negotiating over a corpse's silence.

chapters.title: The Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Ulyana triggers Meridian's full confession across both fleets' channels, but pairs it with proof that the corporations, not either fleet, authored the forged incident. Fleets hold fire, aimed instead at a common enemy. POV: ensemble. Beat: terrifying exposure—justice detonated outside any law.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, both fleets demand a scapegoat. Ulyana negotiates the new truce by offering the one thing they'll accept: the erasure of Ulyana Thackeray—records, registry, name. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief and resolve; survival purchased with self-annihilation.

chapters.title: No Longer Speaking
chapters.summary: Unregistered and unnamed, Ulyana takes a small ship onto a longer, lonelier route, Meridian's final fragment riding in his cargo bay—a witness kept safe rather than silenced. POV: Ulyana. Beat: quiet, hard-won peace; justice done, identity surrendered, the route open ahead.
